summary: Anil Vidyalankar worked in linguistics, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya, Columbia University, and the University of Delhi (PhD). In 1988 he founded Sandhaan, where he served as director (attested 1999).
Ankita Chakraborty is an Indology scholar who studied under doctoral supervisor Bijoya Goswami (attested 2026). She served as a research scholar/fellow at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

Ankur Barua works in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He earned degrees from the Manipal Academy of Higher Education (MD 2003), Sikkim Manipal University (MBAIT 2007), and the University of Hong Kong (MBuddStud 2009) under supervisor Dorothy C. Wong, later holding a post at the University of Delhi (attested 2012).

Ann Appleby Hazlewood worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. She earned a Master of Arts at the Australian National University (attested 1983), where she studied under supervisors Tissa Rajapatirana and Luise Hercus.
Ann Gleig works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at Rice University under the supervision of Jeffrey J. Kripal (attested 2010).

Ann Grodzins Gold is an Indology and religious studies scholar. She earned her BA, MA, and PhD in anthropology at the University of Chicago (~1968–1984). She held posts at Cornell University (~1985–1993) and Syracuse University (~1993–2020) as Professor of Religion and Anthropology.

Ann Heirman specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. She held a post at the National Fund for Scientific Research (1995–2009) and served as director and permanent member at Ghent University (2003–2012).

Ann Laura Stoler works in history, archaeology, and other fields. She studied at Barnard College (BA ~1968–1972) and Columbia University (MA ~1972–1976). She taught at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1983–1989) and University of Michigan (1989–2004), and became Gründungsdirektorin at The New School in 2004.
Anna Andreeva specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She has held posts at Heidelberg University and Ghent University, where she is a permanent member (attested 2026).

Anna Aurelia Esposito is an Indologist who studied at Würzburg, Heidelberg, and Tübingen (MA 1998). She was an assistant professor at the University of Würzburg (attested 2012–2015) and holds a post at the University of Zurich (attested 2026).

Anna Balikci Denjongpa works in Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at SOAS University of London under Lionel Caplan, and also studied with traditional teachers Lopen Dugyal and Gorlok Tulku. In 2002, she became research coordinator at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology.

Anna Brown works in religious studies and other fields. She was a Zen student under Robert Kennedy and has served at Saint Peter's University as chair of political science and director of the social justice program (attested 2017).

Anna Filigenzi is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. She joined the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East in 1984, directed the Italian Archaeological Mission in Afghanistan (2003), and held posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~2012) and Federico II (attested 2021).
Anna M. Shields is a sinologist. She held academic posts at the University of Maryland, College Park (~2007–2015) and Princeton University (~2015).
Anna Morpurgo Davies was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. She studied at Sapienza University of Rome (~1955–1959) and held a post at the University of Oxford (~1964–2004).

Anna Sawerthal is a Tibetologist who earned an MA at the University of Vienna under Klaus-Dieter Mathes and Johanna Buß, and completed a PhD at Heidelberg University, also studying with Dawa Tsering and Norbu Tashi.

Anna Seidel was a scholar of sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Munich, Hamburg, and under Max Kaltenmark and Rolf Alfred Stein. She held posts at the EFEO (1969), the Institut du Hōbōgirin (~1969–1991), and was a visiting professor at Hawaiʻi (1978) and UCSB (1988).

Anna Szabolcsi is a linguist who studied at Eötvös Loránd University and the Hungarian Academy of Sciences (PhD). She worked at the Hungarian Research Centre for Linguistics (~1976–1989), UCLA (~1990–1998), and became professor of linguistics at New York University (~1998).

Anna-Pya Sjödin specializes in Indology and philosophy. She completed her PhD at Uppsala University (2007), where she was supervised by Gunilla Gren-Eklund, Eli Franco, Jonardon Ganeri, K. Venugopalan, and Toshihiro Wada, and also studied under Barbro Eriksson.

Anne C. Klein is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned degrees from Binghamton, Wisconsin-Madison (MA), and Virginia (PhD under Jeffrey Hopkins), while studying with multiple traditional teachers. She held posts at Harvard Divinity School (~1981–1982) and Rice University (~1987).
